name: Oath-Anchor Stones

rarity.note: Hedge-craft of the wave-oath tradition: real, small, and taken seriously.

summary: Palm-sized stones from the Bone Archipelago's skeleton coasts, used to anchor serious promises: both parties hold the stone in salt water and speak the terms. A promise kept leaves the stone warm; a promise broken leaves it cold forever, and cold stones are shown around. Not magic enough for the Censer's lists, not mundane enough to lie about — the space between is where trade lives.
origin: Storm-Bound tradition, older than the order; adopted by harbor-traders everywhere
current_whereabouts: Harbor counting-houses, ship strongboxes, and the pockets of people who intend to keep their word.
properties: Warm when its sworn terms are being kept by all parties; cold when any is broken
One stone, one oath — re-swearing on the same stone muddies both readings
Skeleton-coast stone only; inland rock holds nothing
keepers: Storm-Bound brokers certify genuine anchors; the Skeleton Courts swear theirs on stolen ones out of spite.
value_or_danger: Five shards honest. As evidence in contract court: whatever the dispute is worth.
adventure_hooks: A charter-stone goes cold mid-voyage with everyone aboard keeping their word — something else signed it too.
Players find a cold stone from an oath sworn fifty years ago; finding who broke it settles a fortune.
